FPMC adds a long-term user–candidate dot product to a recent-item–candidate transition score; basket prediction averages transitions from the previous basket. Fossil replaces the explicit long-term user vector with a normalized sum of historical item embeddings, then adds higher-order Markov terms with user-specific plus global lag weights. Thus, combining pooled history with recent-item embeddings has substantial precedent; Fossil’s recent component preserves lag distinctions rather than taking an unweighted mean. [FPMC](https://www.iw3c2.org/papers/2025-Factorizing-Personalized-Markov-Chains.pdf), [Fossil](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152).

Ordinary SASRec already combines recent and older interactions through causal attention, positional embeddings, and residual connections; its final hidden state is a contextual sequence representation, not an explicit stable user vector. A proposed extension h′ = h + g(h,m₅) ⊙ m₅, with m₅ the padding-masked mean of the latest five item embeddings, introduces a direct similarity pathway and context-dependent mixing. These papers motivate that design but do not establish the exact gated five-item residual’s effectiveness. [SASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781).

Suggested inexpensive controls: ordinary SASRec; SASRec plus last-item residual; plus ungated five-item mean; plus five-item mean with a learned global scalar; and the context-gated five-item mean. Match embedding scales, training settings, checkpoint selection, and tuning budgets. Also score last-item similarity and five-item similarity alone. Replace the recent five with five earlier or randomly selected historical items to test recency. Shuffling within a mean-pooled window changes nothing, so cannot demonstrate order sensitivity. Compare paired validation outcomes and per-category HR@10 alongside the common macro average. Gains over last-item controls support multi-item context; gains over scalar mixing support adaptive gating; gains over nonrecent pooling support recency, without establishing order-sensitive transitions.
